text:
sqlpipe moves relational data into object storage as a three-stage pipeline, with each stage running as its own process and communicating over bounded channels so that backpressure propagates naturally from sink to source.

The reader opens a Postgres connection, executes the extraction query with a server-side cursor, and emits fixed-size batches of rows. Bounding the batch size keeps memory flat regardless of table size.

The converter consumes those batches and encodes them into Parquet row groups, applying the column types and compression settings resolved once at startup. Row groups are flushed as soon as they reach the configured target size, so the converter never buffers a whole file.

The uploader takes completed byte ranges and writes them to S3 as multipart upload parts, retrying individual parts with exponential backoff. The upload is committed only after every part succeeds, so a failed run leaves no partial object behind.
